analyses.failure: CHK-012 (assertion) — Issued AXI requests use supported sizes and are aligned: 10 fails / 48986 hits, all in xrand.s1 (base.s1, base.s2, ids8.s1, ids35.s1 have 0 fails). First fail 950000 ps. All 10 fails are inside test_chk_021_accept_qualifiers (0–7465 ns): sim_runs/xrand.s1.log:79 @950000, :85-88 @1430000-1460000 (4 consecutive edges), :93 @1860000, :128-131 @5170000-5200000 (4 consecutive edges). Final count is at xrand.s1.log:3940 'NNC_CHECK CHK-012 hits=9767 fails=10'; base.s1.log:3930 has fails=0.
analyses.spec_says: spec/AHB2AXI_Bridge_Design_Specification.md:313 (rule AA-T1.7.3.1-04, rules.json:2766-2771): "Supported HSIZE encodings are byte, halfword and word (0, 1, 2). Transfer addresses shall be naturally aligned to HSIZE." spec :413 (AA-9-04, rules.json:4044-4049): "HSIZE/AxSIZE 0=1 byte, 1=2 bytes, 2=4 bytes. Larger sizes are rejected." spec :411: "AXI address equals the corresponding accepted AHB address." spec :434 OP-WR-SINGLE: SINGLE/undefined-INCR/Device beats give "One AWLEN=0, one W beat" for that transfer. contract.json:685 (CHK-012): "if o_axi_awvalid=1 then o_axi_awsize <= 2 and o_axi_awaddr mod 2^o_axi_awsize = 0". Reset text: spec :467 says only "FIFO payload contents need not be reset; pointer and validity state are cleared by the shared reset". It allows unreset FIFO payload, but it does not allow an issued AXI request to carry uninitialised controller state.
analyses.rtl_does: The only AW payload source that is not reset is the burst-capture register file. m_ahb2axi_ctrl.sv:123-127 declares `logic [31:0] reg_burst_addr [0:15]; logic [2:0] reg_burst_size [0:15]; logic [2:0] reg_burst_type [0:15]; logic [6:0] reg_burst_prot [0:15]; logic reg_burst_nonsec [0:15];`. None of these is in the reset branch at ctrl.sv:754-779, which resets reg_cmd_*, reg_burst_count/widx/fallback and the others, but not the arrays. They are written only at ctrl.sv:828-832 (slot 0, and only `if (w_idle_cmd_eligible & ~w_idle_cmd_err)`, i.e. an eligible Normal Write-back fixed write burst) and at ctrl.sv:844-848 (w_cap_pop in WR_CAPTURE). In ENUM_ST_WR_SINGLE, ctrl.sv:688-690 drives `if (reg_burst_fallback) begin w_axi_aw_addr = reg_burst_addr[reg_burst_widx[3:0]]; w_axi_aw_size = reg_burst_size[reg_burst_widx[3:0]];`. m_ahb2axi_axi_if.sv:107/109/114 passes these straight to o_axi_awaddr/o_axi_awsize, with AWVALID = i_rst_n_core & i_req_aw_valid. reg_burst_fallback is 1 for every NONSEQ write, including non-eligible SINGLE/INCR/Device writes. w_cap_stop (ctrl.sv:513-516) is not gated by state and is 1 whenever the wr-cmd FIFO head is not a SEQ write. ctrl.sv:859-862 (`if (w_cap_stop) ... reg_burst_fallback <= 1'b1;`) comes after the start block's `reg_burst_fallback <= 1'b0` (ctrl.sv:825), so it wins on the start edge. A non-eligible write therefore goes IDLE→WR_SINGLE with fallback=1 and widx=0, and AWADDR/AWSIZE come from reg_burst_addr[0]/reg_burst_size[0], which were never loaded for that transfer. In base runs those flops start at 0: AWADDR=0, AWSIZE=0 is aligned and size 0, so CHK-012 passes and the wrong address goes unseen. With +verilator+rand+reset+2 (xrand.s1.log:35) they start random, so AWSIZE can be 3..7 or AWADDR misaligned, and CHK-012 fires. The fail at 950 ns (about cycle 95, clock period 10 ns, see CHK-020 fails every 10000 ps) is at the start of the third stimulus phase of test_chk_021, before the first AR handshake at monitor t=101 (xrand.s1.log:46). This fits the first AW of that phase being a non-eligible NONSEQ write that reads an unloaded slot 0. The runs of 4 consecutive failing edges (1430-1460 ns, 5170-5200 ns) fit AWVALID being held with the same stale payload while waiting for AWREADY. The fails stop after 5200 ns, which fits the accessed slots being overwritten with legal values by later eligible WB INCR4 captures (ctrl.sv:828-829, 844-845). After that, the stale values are aligned and size ≤2, so the fault is masked as in base. Ruled out: the AR path uses reg_cmd_addr/reg_cmd_size (ctrl.sv:672/674), which are reset (755-756) and loaded from FIFO entries that were written and validated. The non-fallback AW path uses the same reg_cmd_* (ctrl.sv:695-696). The resetless FIFO read register (m_vlsit_sfifo_mem.sv:48, 59-61) feeds only reg_cmd_* via valid, non-empty entries, so it cannot give an unsupported size or a misaligned address for an accepted, validated transfer. Relation to triage.md: this is a symptom of the ungated w_cap_stop / forced reg_burst_fallback defect (ctrl.sv:513-516 plus 859-862). triage.md describes it as defect 2 in §2 (CHK-022), the 'second issue' in §3 (CHK-023: 'WR_SINGLE then drives AWADDR/AWSIZE/... from reg_burst_addr[0]/reg_burst_size[0]... which were never loaded ... This would show next as a CHK-040 address mismatch'), §8 (CHK-005) and §10 (CHK-016: 'sends a stale reg_burst_addr[0] as AWADDR'). It is not mainly the ahb_if o_req_valid/o_rsp_ready ordering bug (§1). That bug can add to it, because after a desync, WR_SINGLE with fallback and widx>0 can read slots that w_cap_pop never filled, which are also unreset.
analyses.test_does: Checker: verif/sva/nnc_chk_axi.sv:196-201. `a_CHK_012: assert property (@(posedge i_clk_core) disable iff (!i_rst_n_core) (o_axi_arvalid || o_axi_awvalid) |-> ((!o_axi_arvalid || (o_axi_arsize <= 3'd2 && ((o_axi_araddr & ar_mask) == 32'd0))) && (!o_axi_awvalid || (o_axi_awsize <= 3'd2 && ((o_axi_awaddr & aw_mask) == 32'd0)))))`. The masks are at :132-133 (`(32'd1 << o_axi_awsize) - 32'd1`). This is a direct encoding of contract.json:685, and it is disabled during reset. Stimulus at the failing times: test_chk_021 third phase, verif/tests/test_ahb2axi_bridge.py:696-700. Each of 24 groups is `mk(r, r.randrange(2), r.choice((INCR, INCR4)), r.randrange(3), r.choice(LEGAL_MT), n=r.randint(1, 6), busy=0.5)`: reads and writes, sizes 0..2 only, memory types from LEGAL_MT = (DEV_NE, DEV_E, WB_A, WB_B) (line 19). Addresses come from rand_addr (lines 405-408), which masks to natural alignment: `a & ~((1 << size) - 1)`. So every AHB transfer driven is legal, size ≤2 and aligned. No expected AXI value is computed by the test. The SVA expects any issued AW to carry the accepted transfer's legal size and aligned address. The run differs from base.s1 only in x_init=random (run_set.json:8: "a check that passes only because flops start at 0 fails here"; xrand.s1.log:5/35: --x-initial unique, +verilator+rand+reset+2).

candidates.evidence_for: The AW payload in WR_SINGLE with reg_burst_fallback=1 comes from reg_burst_addr/size[widx] (ctrl.sv:688-690). These arrays (ctrl.sv:123-127) have no reset (absent from ctrl.sv:754-779) and are loaded only for eligible WB bursts (ctrl.sv:827-832) or capture pops (843-848). fallback is forced to 1 for every NONSEQ write by the ungated w_cap_stop (ctrl.sv:513-516), whose assignment at 859-862 overrides the clear at 825. So non-eligible writes issue an AW built from state never loaded for that transfer. The AHB stimulus is all legal and aligned (test lines 405-408, 698), so the only way AWSIZE>2 or a misaligned AWADDR can appear is through such state. The failure appears only when that state starts random (xrand). In base it starts at 0 and the defect hides as AWADDR=0/AWSIZE=0, which also violates spec :411 (AXI address equals the AHB address). That already matches the AW-address and BRESP-keying symptoms in triage.md §3 and §10. The first fail (950 ns) comes before any AR of the phase, i.e. before any eligible burst could have loaded slot 0. The fails stop after about 5200 ns, consistent with the slots later being overwritten with legal values.
candidates.evidence_against: No waveform is available, so the exact AWSIZE/AWADDR values and the widx at each failing edge are not logged. Whether a given fail reads slot 0 (forced fallback on a non-eligible write) or a slot >0 left unfilled after a desync from the ahb_if.sv:87-88 drop is inferred from the code and timing. Both paths read the same unreset arrays.

candidates.evidence_for: The failure appears only with random x-initialisation, a simulation-only configuration. One could argue the run models a condition the design was not written for.
candidates.evidence_against: The assertion is a direct encoding of contract.json:685 and is disabled during reset (nnc_chk_axi.sv:197). The stimulus is legal: sizes 0..2, naturally aligned addresses (test lines 405-408, 698). Random power-up values of non-reset flops are physically real. run_set.json:8 defines xrand specifically to expose checks that pass only because flops start at 0. The checker passes 9767 other hits in the same run.

candidates.evidence_for: spec :467 says "FIFO payload contents need not be reset", so a designer could read it as allowing resetless datapath storage in general.
candidates.evidence_against: reg_burst_* are controller registers, not FIFO payload. Even for FIFO payload, :467 relies on the payload being consumed only when valid. Spec :313, :411 and :413 are explicit: AXI requests carry the accepted AHB address and a size of 0..2. No spec text allows an issued AW to carry uninitialised or unrelated state.

analyses.options: Fix RTL (m_ahb2axi_ctrl.sv). This is the same fault as the forced-fallback defect in triage.md §2/§3/§8/§10, not a new one. (1) Root-cause fix: gate w_cap_stop to reg_fsm_ctrl_current_state==ENUM_ST_WR_CAPTURE (ctrl.sv:513-516), or at least stop the `if (w_cap_stop) reg_burst_fallback <= 1'b1` at ctrl.sv:859-862 from overriding the start-edge clear at 825. Non-eligible SINGLE/INCR/Device writes then take the reg_cmd_* path (ctrl.sv:695-698), which is reset and loaded with the accepted transfer. (2) Make sure the fallback path can only index slots that capture actually filled: reg_burst_widx < reg_burst_count, and reg_burst_count cleared for non-eligible starts. This covers the desync case caused by the ahb_if.sv:87-88 ordering bug, which should also be fixed as in triage §1. (3) Optional hardening: reset reg_burst_addr/size/type/prot/nonsec (ctrl.sv:123-127) in the reset branch at 754-779. This alone is not a fix, because base runs show that zero-valued stale entries give the wrong AWADDR=0 (spec :411) without tripping CHK-012. After the fix, re-run xrand.s1 and base. CHK-012 in xrand and the CHK-016 and AW-address mismatches in base are expected to change together. No test change is indicated. Optionally clarify the spec at :467 to say that only FIFO payload may be resetless and that no AXI request may be built from storage not written for that transfer. Do not relax CHK-012 or exclude the xrand configuration.
